# Struct layout format

A stream whose messages have a fixed binary layout declares it in
`streams.toml` (see [Configuration](../concepts/configuration.md)), and
every recording stores it, so the recording can be decoded without the
configuration it was made with.

## In a recording

The stream's MCAP channel has message encoding `kapto.struct/v1`: each
message is the payload exactly as received. The channel's schema has
encoding `kapto.struct/v1`, the stream's name as its name, and the
layout as JSON as its data. Streams without a layout are stored with
message encoding `kapto.raw` and no schema.

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "sequence",
      "type": "u32",
      "offset": 0,
      "count": 1,
      "byte_order": "little",
      "scale": null,
      "unit": null
    },
    {
      "name": "joint_positions",
      "type": "i32",
      "offset": 4,
      "count": 7,
      "byte_order": "big",
      "scale": 0.001,
      "unit": "rad"
    }
  ]
}
```

Every key is always written. A reader requires `name`, `type` and
`offset`; `count` defaults to 1, `byte_order` to `little`, and `scale`
and `unit` to none.

## Fields

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter; unique in the layout. |
| `type` | One of the types below. |
| `offset` | Byte offset of the first value in the message. |
| `count` | Number of values one after another: 1 for a single value, more for an array. |
| `byte_order` | `little` (least significant byte first) or `big`. |
| `scale` | Multiplier applied to each value, e.g. 0.001 for a value sent in thousandths. Scaled values are decimals. Not allowed on `bool`. |
| `unit` | The unit of the (scaled) value, e.g. `rad`. |

Every field must end within 65,507 bytes, the largest UDP message.
Fields may overlap. Bytes no field covers are ignored, and a message
shorter than the end of the last field is not decoded (it is still
recorded).

## Types

| Type | Bytes |
|---|---|
| `u8` | 1 |
| `i8` | 1 |
| `u16` | 2 |
| `i16` | 2 |
| `u32` | 4 |
| `i32` | 4 |
| `u64` | 8 |
| `i64` | 8 |
| `f32` | 4 |
| `f64` | 8 |
| `bool` | 1 |

Integers decode as integers unless scaled, so 64-bit values keep every
digit. A `bool` is one byte: 0 is false, anything else true.
